The later comma after Бергоньоне marks the modifier boundary before он; do not treat every visible comma as a modifier boundary. The retained label выделяется запятыми с двух сторон names that treatment. A single comma before the phrase would omit its closing boundary in this supplied sentence.

In Написанная в спешке программа выполнила недопустимую операцию. The same descriptive phrase precedes the noun. The supplied example has no separating commas: запятые не ставятся is its label. Phrase position helps distinguish these two examples; this does not mean commas are never used before a described noun.

The retained rule states exceptions when the described entity is a personal pronoun or the participial phrase expresses a cause. Воспитанный в традициях Фоппы, Бернардо Дзенале и Амброджо Бергоньоне, он прошёл обучение в мастерской Леонардо. The opening phrase describes он, so A separating comma follows the opening participial phrase before the main clause. The comma after Фоппы is internal to the list of names. The later comma after Бергоньоне marks the modifier boundary before он; do not treat every visible comma as a modifier boundary. Изумлённый этим хохотом, Павел сел на пол и смотрел куда-то в угол The retained source row explicitly gives this example a causal shade, so A separating comma follows the opening participial phrase before the main clause. The ordinary preceding-noun label запятые не ставятся cannot cancel these exceptions. The optional source wording личным местоимением and кроме тех случаев identifies a category/connective, not a complete comma decision; its reference question does not satisfy these language checks.

Туча, нависшая над высокими вершинами тополей, уже сыпала дождиком The phrase describes Туча and is followed by the continuing predicate, so Separating commas mark both boundaries of the participial phrase before the sentence continues. Вдали виднеется маяк, стоящий у моря Here the phrase describes маяк and ends the supplied construction, so A separating comma precedes the terminal participial phrase, with no closing comma at sentence end. A closing separating comma would have no continuing clause after it. By contrast, No separating comma is used between the participial phrase and the word it describes. is the ordinary non-causal, non-pronoun preceding-noun default shown in the earlier program example. These are bounded supplied constructions; not every phrase before a noun needs a comma and not every phrase after a word fits one universal rule.

The retained но́вый and нов both mean new. The first is the long form and the second is the masculine singular short form. The grammatical check asks which form is shown, rather than its English gloss. Long adjectives have case, gender and number inflection; short adjectives vary for gender and number, not case. The retained examples are recognition targets, not a universal rule for producing short forms by removing endings.

In the taught modern use, short adjectives occur only in the nominative and are used predicatively to describe their subject. A long adjective can modify a noun attributively and can also be a predicate. The choice depends on the sentence, not a universal rule about one fixed word position. The following supplied forms, complete clauses and noun phrases support bounded agreement and function checks; they do not settle every long-versus-short semantic or stylistic choice.

The retained беж means beige and is an invariant colour form, unchanged for case, gender and number. Its short appearance does not make it the short counterpart of но́вый. Keep lexical meaning, inflection and adjective function separate. The correct glosses remain in Vocabulary Lab as word-meaning practice; they do not satisfy the independent adjective grammar checks.

The supplied short forms of new are нов for masculine singular, нова́ for feminine singular, но́во for neuter singular and новы́ for plural. Short adjectives agree with their subject in gender and number; they do not have a modern case paradigm. In the retained noun examples, книга is feminine singular, письмо is neuter singular, and книги has the supplied plural reading. Choose the short form for that subject rather than another form with the same lexical meaning. Some adjectives lack short forms and stress can change; these supplied forms are not a universal truncation recipe.

The complete clauses Поезд старый and Студент новый say that the train is old and the student is new. Their long adjectives predicate a property of the subject. No overt present copula appears in these supplied clauses. Long form therefore does not force attributive function, and a temporary-versus-permanent slogan does not decide every form choice. Read the whole example and its supplied meaning rather than its adjective ending alone.

The supplied новый карандаш and новое письмо mean new pencil and new letter. Each is an attributive noun phrase: the adjective modifies the head noun. These phrases alone do not assert that a pencil or letter is new in a complete clause. The adjective and noun agree in gender and number in the supplied singular examples. Do not infer an exceptionless word-position rule or every possible case from an isolated phrase. These exercises assess bounded agreement and function recognition, not unrestricted production or every long/short meaning distinction.

Когда причастный оборот стоит перед определяемым словом, запятые не ставятся, кроме тех случаев, когда определяемое слово выражено личным местоимением или причастный оборот обозначает причину. Если после причастного оборота конец предложения, то запятая ставится только перед причастным оборотом.

'''Примеры:'''
* ''Программа, написанная в спешке, выполнила недопустимую операцию.''

exactSpan=The active past participle is used in order to indicate actions that happened in the past:
:Де́вушка, '''чита́вшая''' тут кни́гу, забы́ла свой телефо́н – The girl '''that read''' this book here forgot her phone (the girl read the book '''in the past''').

Compare:
:Де́вушка, '''чита́ющая''' тут кни́гу, – моя́ сестра́ – The girl '''reading''' this book here is my sister (she is reading the book now, '''in the present''').

exactSpan=В русском языке причастный оборот часто выделяется [[Запятая|запятыми]]. Если причастный оборот стоит после определяемого слова, он выделяется запятыми с двух сторон. Когда причастный оборот стоит перед определяемым словом, запятые не ставятся, кроме тех случаев, когда определяемое слово выражено личным местоимением или причастный оборот обозначает причину. Если после причастного оборота конец предложения, то запятая ставится только перед причастным оборотом.

'''Примеры:'''
* ''Программа, написанная в спешке, выполнила недопустимую операцию.''
* ''Написанная в спешке программа выполнила недопустимую операцию.
